title: Influence of dietary supplementation with maritime pine bark extract (Pycnogenol®) on the sensitivity of the glycocalyx of erythrocytes to sodium
summary:
Pycnogenol® is an extract from the French maritime pine, which is available as a dietary supplement. It contains a mixture of water-soluble, naturally occurring bioflavonoids and fruit acids. Bioflavonoids act as antioxidants and have various health-promoting properties similar to those of vitamins. Pycnogenol® is said to have numerous positive effects, including a blood pressure-lowering and antioxidant effect. This means that it can scavenge highly reactive and potentially harmful molecules that are produced, for example, as part of inflammatory processes.
High blood pressure is a widespread disease characterized by permanently increased pressure in the blood vessels. In the long term, this can damage the blood vessels and increase the risk of secondary diseases such as heart attacks, strokes or kidney damage. High salt consumption (sodium chloride, NaCl) can contribute to the development of high blood pressure, although not everyone is equally sensitive to salt. Around a third of people show an increased sensitivity to salt, which can now be determined by a simple capillary blood test from the finger.
A little table salt is added to a blood sample and the sedimentation rate of the red blood cells is measured in a thin tube. A special layer on the cell surface, the so-called glycocalyx, surrounds the blood cells like a protective cushion. If salt sensitivity is high, this layer is damaged by the salt and loses its structure, causing the blood cells to sink more quickly. A particularly high salt sensitivity is present if the test result is 20% or more above the norm - the higher the value, the more sensitive a person is to foods high in salt.
It is not yet clear whether certain plant-based ingredients in food can influence salt sensitivity. The aim of this study is therefore to find out whether taking Pycnogenol® for seven days influences the salt sensitivity of red blood cells.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy men/women aged 18 to 65 years
Signed informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Any known systemic diseases or regular drug treatment
Course of antibiotic treatment within the past 4 weeks
Intake of dietary supplements
Pregnant and breastfeeding women
